oom-isolation.scope: Out-of-memory isolation for Claude Code sessions added in 1.2.4 (firehose PR #754). On Linux, when tmux runs a pane in a systemd tmux-spawn-*.scope (tmux 3.4 built with systemd support), an out-of-memory kill of any process in the scope used to stop the whole scope, ending the Claude session and removing it from the sidebar. Firehose now starts its own scope with OOMPolicy=continue for each Claude process it finds in such a scope (through busctl --user StartTransientUnit) and moves the rest of the pane's processes into it, so an out-of-memory kill stops only the process the kernel chose. It runs during session discovery and on a server timer every 15 seconds, covers Claude Code only (getClaudeProcesses), does nothing on macOS, stops trying when busctl is missing, leaves Claude in place when a move fails, and is turned off by CM_CLAUDE_OOM_ISOLATION=0 (not documented for readers). Process discovery also keeps partial lsof output when one process exits mid-scan. Source inspection and the PR's recorded live test only; no out-of-memory kill was observed for this documentation.

chat-history-snapshots.scope: Chat fix in 1.2.5 (firehose PR #759) for Claude Code 2.1.300, published 2026-10-14, which began writing internal API request snapshots (api-request-blob records) into its transcript. Firehose 1.2.4 and earlier showed them as chat messages without a message id, duplicating tool activity; the next send then threw in optimistic-message cleanup before the request reached the server, while the message box still cleared, so the message looked sent but was never delivered. 1.2.5 drops those records from the conversation (lib/jsonl-parser.ts) and tolerates rows without an id already loaded in the dashboard (optimisticMessages.ts). Source inspection and the PR's tests only; not reproduced against a real Claude Code 2.1.300 session.

update-command.scope: firehose version and firehose update at 1.2.5. firehose version prints 'firehose <version> (<distribution>, <channel>[, build <id>])' followed by the update notice (present since at least 1.2.2; the notice since 1.2.3). firehose update fetches the release index, downloads the newer archive, verifies its sha256, unpacks it under releases/<version>, and switches to it, logging '[update] Firehose <current> is up to date (latest <latest>)' or '[update] Firehose <latest> is available (running <current>)', then '[update] Now running <latest>'. The switch restarts a service-managed server (or a hand-started one through the restart transaction) and flips back to the previous release if the new one is not healthy. Conversation history is parsed on the server with an in-memory cache (lib/parse-cache.ts), so a restart after the 1.2.5 update re-reads Claude transcripts without the internal records. Source inspection only; no update was run for this documentation.
